After reaching 0, push the "Down" button to remember the parameters. Move the blade to the top position and remove the Vibrocheck block. Slicing procedure (done in the chemical hood): Put the Whatman filter paper 90 mm into the 100 mm Petri dish and place the dish on ice. Prepare the single edge, carbon steel blade. Prepare surgical instruments: scissors, small mini-scissors, tweezers, spatula, and Pasteur cut pipette. Bring the mouse from the animal facility. Check the temperature of the solutions. Take the black buffer tray and specimen holder from the freezer and place the black buffer tray on ice. Wipe the specimen holder. Note: The holder should be completely dry. Place a small amount of instant tissue adhesive on the center of the specimen holder. Fill the Petri dish with cold slicing solution (step A1). Put two weighing dishes near the surgical instruments. Fill two weighing dishes with cold slicing solution. The next steps have to be performed in accordance with the Institutional and National Animal Care regulations. Measure 0.5 mL of isoflurane and distribute it over the towel attached to the cover of the exicator. Cover the exicator. Put the animal into the exicator and quickly cover it. Wait a minute for the isoflurane to take effect. Take a mouse and cut the skin from its head to expose the skull. Cut the head close to occipital bone with scissors. Wash the head in the first weighing dish with cold slicing solution for a few seconds. Cut the bone with surgical scissors as follows: i. Insert the surgical scissors through the foramen magnum in the occipital bone. ii. Continue along the occipital bone until the end of the lacrimal bone. iii. Cut down from the lacrimal's end to the eye cavity. Gently remove the cut bone with tweezers and expose the brain. Put the brain into the second weighing dish with ice-cold slicing solution. Transfer the brain into a Petri dish. Cut the block of the brain (coronal or sagittal plane). Paste it in the specimen holder. Transfer the holder to a buffer tray. Insert the buffer tray into the insert in the vibratome. Fill the buffer tray with an ice-cold slicing solution. Cut the first thick slice. Discard the slice. Adjust to 300 µm slice thickness and cut the slice. Remove the slice with a paintbrush. Collect the slice with a cut Pasteur pipette. Transfer the slice to a warm incubation solution (step A2). Repeat until the desired number of slices is cut. Incubate the slices for 60 min. Caution: It is advisable to perform steps 4r–4ee with maximum speed, ideally completing them in under 1 min. More extended periods of ischemia/hypoxia could cause irreversible damage to the brain tissue. Whole-cell recording and filling neurons with fluorescent dye (always document the experiment in a lab book) Turn on all equipment and perfuse aCSFx1 through the slice mini chamber. Set the temperature under the objective to 32 °C using the temperature controller. Transfer a 300 µm thick slice from the incubating chamber to the slice mini chamber and put a platinum grid to pin down the slice. Focus on Layer 5 cell body layer (approximately 500–700 µm below the pial surface). Identify an L5 Pyramidal neuron to patch using the 60× objective. Do not move the X and Y position of the microscope from this point on. Pull two pipettes by using the P-97 micropipette puller. Note that the pipette resistance should be 10–12 MΩ when filled with K + -based intracellular solution or 7–9 MΩ when filled with aCSF. Note that optimal pipette size may vary depending on the specific preparations. Cut a 4–5 mm wide, 10 mm long strip of Parafilm. Wrap the pipette with one or two layers of Parafilm, ~1 mm from the tip, to reduce the pipette stray capacitance. Fill the first pipette with K + -based intracellular solution supplemented with SBFI (2 mM). Fill the other pipette with aCSFx1 supplemented with SBFI (2 mM). Place both pipettes in the micromanipulator pipette holders. Apply gentle positive pressure, place the pipettes in the bath, focus on their tips, and move them down, one by one, toward the surface of the slice. Stop moving the pipettes before approaching the cell; ensure that the cell body is below the whole-cell pipette. Set the Multiclamp-700B Commander Channels 1 and 2 to voltage-clamp mode and correct the pipette offset. Apply a seal test, a -10 mV voltage step, to both pipettes. Approach the cell body with the first pipette by moving it along the z-axis until a dimple appears on the membrane. Release the positive pressure and apply gentle suction while monitoring the current response to the voltage step until the gigaohmic seal forms. Move the holding voltage to -70 mV and correct fast capacitance using automatic correction of the Commander. Apply gentle and brief suction pulse with a syringe to break into whole-cell configuration (or by mouth). The successful break-in is evident by an abrupt increase in the amplitude of capacitative transients in response to -10 mV voltage steps. Switch the Commander to the Current Clamp mode. Correct the Bridge. A Current Clamp whole-cell recording is established for pipette

steps.title: Prepare aCSF ×10 stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve for 1 L: NaCl 1240 mM (72.466 g), KCl 30 mM (2.237 g), NaHCO₃ 260 mM (21.843 g), NaH₂PO₄ 12.5 mM (1.725 g). Mix with distilled water, adjust volume to 1 L.

steps.title: Make aCSF working solution
steps.instruction: Combine 100 mL aCSF ×10 stock, 10 mL 1 M D‑glucose (final 10 mM), 2 mL 1 M MgSO₄ (final 2 mM), ~850 mL distilled water, bubble with 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂ for 15 min, add 2 mL 1 M CaCl₂ (final 2 mM), adjust final volume to 1 L.

steps.title: Prepare 1 M MgSO₄ stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10.165 g MgSO₄·7H₂O in distilled water and bring volume to 50 mL.

steps.title: Prepare 1 M CaCl₂ stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 7.352 g CaCl₂·2H₂O in distilled water and bring volume to 50 mL.

steps.title: Prepare K⁺ intracellular solution
steps.instruction: For 100 mL: dissolve 3.045 g K‑gluconate (130 mM), add 0.6 mL 1 M KCl (6 mM), 0.2 mL 1 M MgCl₂ (2 mM), 1 mL 1 M HEPES (10 mM), 0.4 mL 1 M NaCl (4 mM), add water to 100 mL, titrate to pH 7.25 with 1 M KOH. No ATP/GTP added.

steps.title: Aliquot SBFI solution
steps.instruction: Add SBFI to intracellular and aCSF solutions to 2 mM, aliquot 100 µL into microtubes and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare slicing aCSF (aCSF ×1)
steps.instruction: Transfer 250 mL freshly prepared aCSF working solution into a 300 mL glass beaker, place on ice, bubble with 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂ for ≥15 min, cover with Parafilm, cool to 4 °C, add 0.7 mL 1 M MgSO₄, add 0.25 mL 1 M CaCl₂ (pre‑bubbled to avoid precipitation), re‑cover.

steps.title: Prepare incubation aCSF
steps.instruction: Transfer 500 mL freshly prepared aCSF ×1 into the slice incubator, bubble with 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂ for ≥15 min, cover, warm to 30 °C, add 0.7 mL 1 M CaCl₂.

steps.title: Set up vibratome
steps.instruction: Place black buffer tray and specimen holder in –20 °C freezer; wash double‑edge feather blade with 70 % ethanol, rinse, dry, insert into holder; install Vibrocheck unit, connect USB; calibrate: ensure green light on Down button, insert Allen screwdriver, rotate 90° CCW until white strip appears, press Down, press Run, adjust display to 0 by turning “‑” screw, press Down to save, move blade to top, remove Vibrocheck block.

steps.title: Prepare slicing station
steps.instruction: Place 90 mm Whatman filter paper in a 100 mm × 15 mm Petri dish on ice; gather single‑edge carbon steel blade, scissors, mini‑scissors, tweezers, spatula, Pasteur cut pipette; keep two weighing dishes filled with cold slicing solution nearby.

steps.title: Anesthetize mouse
steps.instruction: Measure 0.5 mL isoflurane, distribute onto towel covering exicator cover, close exicator, place mouse inside, wait 1 min for anesthesia to take effect.

steps.title: Expose brain
steps.instruction: Cut skin from head to expose skull, cut head near occipital bone with scissors, rinse head in first cold slicing solution dish, insert surgical scissors through foramen magnum, cut along occipital bone to lacrimal bone, cut down to eye cavity, remove bone with tweezers, expose brain, transfer brain to second cold slicing solution dish.

steps.title: Mount brain block
steps.instruction: Transfer brain to a Petri dish, cut a coronal or sagittal block, apply a small drop of instant tissue adhesive to center of specimen holder, paste brain block onto holder, place holder in buffer tray, fill tray with ice‑cold slicing solution.

steps.title: Cut brain slices
steps.instruction: Set vibratome thickness to 300 µm; cut first thick slice and discard; then cut successive 300 µm slices, remove each slice with a paintbrush, collect with cut Pasteur pipette, transfer immediately to warm incubation solution.

substeps.instruction: Perform all steps from mouse removal to slice transfer in ≤1 min to avoid ischemic damage.

steps.title: Incubate slices
steps.instruction: Place slices in warm incubation aCSF (30 °C) for 60 min.

steps.title: Set up recording chamber
steps.instruction: Turn on all equipment, perfuse aCSF ×1 through slice mini‑chamber, set temperature under objective to 32 °C with temperature controller.

steps.title: Pin slice for recording
steps.instruction: Transfer a 300 µm slice from incubator to slice mini‑chamber, secure with a platinum grid, focus on layer‑5 cell‑body layer (≈500–700 µm below pial surface).

steps.title: Pull and prepare pipettes
steps.instruction: Pull two glass pipettes with P‑97 puller; aim for 10–12 MΩ resistance when filled with K⁺ intracellular solution or 7–9 MΩ with aCSF; cut a 4–5 mm × 10 mm Parafilm strip, wrap each pipette ~1 mm from tip with 1–2 layers of Parafilm.

steps.title: Fill recording pipettes
steps.instruction: Fill pipette 1 with K⁺ intracellular solution containing 2 mM SBFI; fill pipette 2 with aCSF ×1 containing 2 mM SBFI.

steps.title: Position pipettes in bath
steps.instruction: Place pipettes in micromanipulator holders, apply gentle positive pressure, lower them into bath, focus on tips, stop before contacting cell; keep X‑Y microscope position fixed.

steps.title: Form whole‑cell configuration
steps.instruction: Set Multiclamp‑700B channels 1 & 2 to voltage‑clamp, correct pipette offset, apply –10 mV seal test; advance pipette 1 toward cell until membrane dimple appears, release pressure, apply gentle suction to obtain gigaohm seal, move holding voltage to –70 mV, perform automatic fast‑capacitance correction, break into whole‑cell (brief suction pulse or mouth suction), switch to current‑clamp, correct bridge.

steps.title: Allow SBFI diffusion
steps.instruction: Wait 15 min after establishing whole‑cell recording to let SBFI diffuse throughout the neuron.

steps.title: Acquire axonal fluorescence image
steps.instruction: Focus NeuroCCD‑SMQ camera on axon, set exposure to 8 ms, illuminate with 385 nm high‑intensity LED, collect emission through U‑MNU2 filter using NeuroPlex software.

steps.title: Select first axonal point
steps.instruction: Choose a point ≈10 µm from soma edge for back‑propagation measurements (or 30–40 µm for forward propagation).

steps.title: Touch axon with pipette 2
steps.instruction: Move pipette 2 to the selected point, gently touch axon (no suction), verify contact by acquiring one or more single frames with NeuroCCD‑SMQ.

steps.title: Stimulate soma and record
steps.instruction: Deliver 2–7 ms current steps via pipette 1, increase amplitude until an action potential is evoked; then deliver 600 steps at 1.5× threshold amplitude, 2–5 Hz, while recording voltage (pipette 1) and axonal current (pipette 2); save recording file.

steps.title: Repeat for additional axonal sites
steps.instruction: Move 10–20 µm further distally along axon, repeat touch, stimulation, and recording; perform for 6–10 sites spanning 10–150 µm from soma.

steps.title: Optional two‑photon morphology
steps.instruction: Turn on Ultima IV two‑photon microscope, perfuse aCSF through slice mini‑chamber, set temperature to 32 °C, transfer SBFI‑labeled slice to Ultima chamber, pin with platinum grid, locate neuron with low‑resolution live scan at 740 nm, acquire Z‑stack of 20–40 images at 0.5–1.0 µm intervals, open stack in ImageJ for morphometric analysis.
